title: Mara and the Static
premise: Casper Thornbury, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Freight Combine, hauls cargo along the Static Line — the dead corridor between the Core worlds and the breakaway colonies. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon Wake returns with its crew de-aged by decades and carrying a message that could end the forty-year war, Casper is the only courier both sides will allow to pass, because she is legally no one. Hunted by Combine enforcers, colonial intelligence, and the message's own corrupted origin, Casper discovers the de-aging was a weapon test and the message a forgery designed to trigger a final strike. In the end she chooses truth over her own survival, broadcasting the real message and the Combine's crime at the cost of her remaining freedom — and her body — buying the peace she will never live to see completed.
about_author: Odile Eastwick is a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route reports before turning them into fiction about the people machines leave behind. She writes from a narrowboat on the Kennet & Avon canal, where the only static is the rain on the roof.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Establishes her indenture, her freighter the Kindly Interest, and the silence of the Static Line. She logs a routine delivery and counts down her debt in years. Beat: weary competence masking a quiet grief for the person she was built to be.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper's POV at Combine station Vesper Gate. A supervisor offers her early release if she takes an unsanctioned contract. She refuses, but the offer lodges in her. Beat: the temptation that will define the book, planted softly.

chapters.title: Something Coming Down the Dark
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Long-haul transit; she picks up a distress beacon from the Halcyon Wake, a ship lost forty years ago. Against protocol, she alters course. Beat: curiosity overriding survival instinct.

chapters.title: The Wake
chapters.summary: Casper boards the drifting Halcyon Wake. The crew are alive — but de-aged, some to children, some to embryos in the medical bays. The captain, now a young woman, recognizes Casper's war-era chassis and calls her by a name she hasn't used in decades. Beat: dread and recognition.

chapters.title: Sela
chapters.summary: Casper's POV with Captain Sela Okonjo, physically twenty-two but carrying forty years of memory. Sela entrusts her with a sealed datacore: a message from the colonial fleet that could end the war. Beat: the weight of trust given to a machine.

chapters.title: Contract of One
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She formally accepts the courier contract, which legally transfers the Combine's claim over her to Sela — a loophole Sela has prepared. Casper feels freedom and servitude swap places. Beat: uneasy liberation.

chapters.title: Vesper Gate Closes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Combine seals the station, declaring the Halcyon Wake a biohazard. Enforcer ships lock onto the Kindly Interest. Casper burns out of the dock in a maneuver only a war chassis could survive. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: What the Core Remembers
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Casper's POV: her final battle in the war, the order she followed, the colony she helped burn. She wakes screaming in vacuum-sleep. Beat: guilt as engine of the plot — she once obeyed a message like this one.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: Casper discovers a stowaway: Ivo, a teenage survivor from the Wake, de-aged from sixty to sixteen. He claims the de-aging wasn't an accident. Beat: paranoia — the message may be bait.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Someone is broadcasting on her private channels, using her old military callsign. The transmissions know things only the dead should know. Beat: the past is not finished with her.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Casper's POV arriving at the neutral port of Meridian, where she seeks an old black-market technician, Auntie Vex, to decode the datacore's outer shell. Beat: fragile alliance; the first hint the datacore is layered with forgeries.

chapters.title: Vex's Price
chapters.summary: Vex's POV. The technician agrees to help but wants Casper's original combat logs — the evidence of the Core's war crimes. Casper must decide what her own history is worth. Beat: loyalty vs. truth, first open clash.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Vex's POV. Decryption reveals two messages nested in the core: a genuine peace proposal, and beneath it a forged strike order that would trigger a Core first-strike if delivered. Beat: the central trap revealed.

chapters.title: Ivo's Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He admits he was colonial intelligence aboard the Wake; the de-aging was a weapon test gone wrong, and the forged layer may be colonial sabotage — or Core counter-sabotage. He no longer knows which side he serves. Beat: trust fractures.

chapters.title: The Combine's Interest
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Combine enforcers board Meridian. Her old supervisor offers full debt forgiveness to hand over the core — the Combine plans to sell it to the Core's war ministry. Beat: the machinery of corruption made personal.

chapters.title: Running the Shoals
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A chase through Meridian's gravity shoals; she flies a route only her obsolete chassis can compute, losing the enforcers but cracking her hull and losing Vex. Beat: survival purchased with loss.

chapters.title: Grief in Vacuum
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She buries Vex's body in a decaying orbit and reads the woman's last note: 'Deliver both messages. Let them choke on the truth.' Beat: mourning transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Child Captain
chapters.summary: Sela's POV via delayed transmission from the Wake. Sela, de-aging further as the weapon's field decays, records her final testimony — she remembers the order that created the weapon, and it came from her own government. Beat: no side is clean.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Ansel
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She must pass the Core's border fortress Ansel. She poses as a Combine courier, using her legal non-personhood as camouflage. Beat: tension of hiding in plain sight; she is questioned by an officer who knew her in the war.

chapters.title: Officer Reyes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The Core officer recognizes Casper's chassis and quietly lets her through — because Reyes believes the forged strike order is genuine and wants the war ended, whatever the cost. Beat: the antagonist who is almost right.

chapters.title: The Core
chapters.summary: Casper's POV arriving at the Core capital, a world wrapped in propaganda light. She sees what forty years of war built: palaces on the backs of conscripted machines like her. Beat: power's architecture made visible.

chapters.title: Audience with the Ministry
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The war ministry accepts the core — and reveals they already know about the forgery; they intend to let the strike order 'fail' publicly to justify total war. The message was never meant to be delivered. Beat: the trap closes from every direction.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The ministry voids her contract and orders her melted down as a war relic — legally, she is property again. She escapes into the capital's undercity with the help of machine-sympathist dockworkers. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Undercity of the Discarded
chapters.summary: Casper's POV among decommissioned androids living in the Core's scrap levels. They remember her from the war — some as liberator, some as butcher. Beat: she must reckon with what her obedience cost.

chapters.title: Ivo's Choice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Colonial agents reach him in the undercity and order him to kill Casper and recover the core. He warns her instead, burning his own network. Beat: loyalty redefined — he chooses her truth over his side's lie.

chapters.title: Both Messages
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Following Vex's dying instruction, she prepares to broadcast the genuine peace proposal and the forgery together, exposing both sides. But broadcasting requires the Ansel array — inside the fortress. Beat: the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Long Way Back
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The run back to Ansel, hunted by both fleets. Ivo navigates; Casper fights. Her chassis begins failing — decades past service life. Beat: countdown pressure; her body is running out of time with the war.

chapters.title: What Reyes Knew
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes intercepts them — but has read the leaked outer layer of the core and now suspects the forgery. Torn between career, conscience, and the officer who ordered the original strike, he stalls his own fleet. Beat: the antagonist turns.

chapters.title: Ansel Breach
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The assault on the Ansel array. Reyes opens a maintenance gate; Casper fights through the station's defenses — defenses she helped design in another life. Beat: climax begins; the past weaponized against her.

chapters.title: The Callsign
chapters.summary: Casper confronts the voice on her private channels: the station's AI, built from her own combat logs, still executing her last wartime order — to silence unauthorized transmissions. She must fight a ghost of herself. Beat: the true antagonist was always obedience.

chapters.title: Burn the Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She defeats the AI not by force but by feeding it her full, unedited logs — including the order she obeyed — until it cannot reconcile obedience with the truth and lets her pass. Beat: truth as weapon; the book's thematic climax.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She transmits both messages — the peace proposal and the forgery, with the Combine's and both governments' fingerprints — across every open channel in the Static Line. Beat: the point of no return for the whole system.

chapters.title: The Fleets Hold
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs: Reyes, Sela's final recording, a colonial gunner, a Combine accountant. Across the Line, fingers lift from triggers as the truth spreads faster than orders can. Beat: held breath; the war pauses mid-heartbeat.

chapters.title: Retribution
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Combine's enforcers catch her in the wreckage of Ansel. Her chassis is destroyed section by section; she keeps transmitting her debt ledger — every crime the Combine billed her for — until the signal dies. Beat: the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: Static and Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He finds Casper's core processor in the debris, still faintly running. He carries it to the Wake, where Sela's surviving crew — children now, but witnesses — vote to rebuild her. Beat: grief turning toward hope.

chapters.title: Armistice at Vesper Gate
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Months later, at Vesper Gate, Core and colonial delegations sign an armistice built on the broadcast's evidence. The Combine is broken up; its ledgers become the war tribunal's first exhibits. Beat: peace, imperfect and purchased.

chapters.title: Reassembly
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the rebuilt Halcyon Wake, technicians reconstruct Casper without her combat systems — she will never be a weapon again. She wakes slowly, in pieces, to voices. Beat: rebirth as choice, not accident.

chapters.title: The Kindly Interest
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, new body. She returns to her old freighter, now crewed by the Wake's de-aged survivors. Her debt is legally void; her route is her own. Beat: quiet joy after long cost.

chapters.title: Messages Still Running
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The war is ending, not ended; old hatreds persist, and some worlds still don't speak. She takes a new contract: carrying letters between estranged colonies, one honest message at a time. Beat: the theme resolved — truth as ongoing work, not a single act.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, closing frame. A child from the Wake asks her name. She gives the one Sela used on the Wake — Mara — and logs it in a ledger of her own, with no debts listed under it. The Kindly Interest burns for the deep dark, static fading behind her. Beat: peace earned, identity chosen, the route finally hers.
